record.what_it_does: Podio is a customizable work/CRM platform (owned by Progress) where teams build apps for items like contacts, deals, and tasks, all exposed through a full REST API.
record.auth_notes: Podio's API uses OAuth2 exclusively for token issuance, with four flows: server-side, client-side, username/password, and 'App authentication' (a service-account-style flow scoped to a single Podio app, using an app ID + app token, recommended over username/password for automated scripts). All requests then carry `Authorization: OAuth2 ACCESS_TOKEN` as a bearer token. There is no separate static API key auth mode — the 'API key' generated in account settings is actually an OAuth2 Client ID/Secret pair used to bootstrap one of these flows.
record.access_notes: Any developer signs up for a free Podio account, generates a Client ID/Secret ('API key') at podio.com/settings/api, and immediately gets working OAuth2 credentials. The free plan includes API access with base rate limits (1,000 calls/hour for standard requests, 250/hour for resource-intensive ones); higher limits require paid add-ons/plans, but baseline access is free and self-serve.
record.main_blocker: rate limits are low on the free tier and the official MCP server is still in beta

record.open_questions: No OpenAPI/Swagger spec was found published by Podio (docs are hand-written HTML), so tooling would need custom schema generation. The official MCP server is explicitly beta and currently exposes only 22 tools (a subset of the full REST API's ~30+ resource areas).
